items.title: Iran's supreme leader killed
items.description: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has been killed in Israeli and US strikes, Iran's state-controlled media has reported.

items.title: Inside the unlikely alliance that broke Trump and unleashed the Epstein files
items.description: Many of Donald Trump's supporters wanted to send those implicated in Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking ring "off to the gallows", but then the president changed his mind about releasing the files. What followed was an unusual political manoeuvre, acts of immense bravery by survivors and a backflip by the president of the United States.

items.title: Why Trump has suddenly developed a taste for attacking other countries
items.description: Trump once proclaimed: "I am especially proud to be the first president in decades who has started no new wars." Now things have changed.

items.title: Joy and grief as Iranian Australians react to US-Israeli airstrikes
items.description: Iranian Australians attend large gatherings around the country to mark the death of Iran's supreme leader in air strikes by the United States and Israel.

items.title: How the internet reacted to Matildas 1-0 win over Philippines
items.description: The Matildas opened their Women's Asian Cup 2026 campaign with a win, beating the Philippines 1-0 in Perth, and the internet watched on with bated breath.

items.title: Perth terror accused revealed as former Christian schoolboy and labourer
items.description: Jayson Joseph Michaels, 20, left school to undertake a TAFE course in IT and worked as a labourer in Bindoon, the ABC can reveal.

items.title: Canadian backpacker's family calls for coronial inquest after death on K'gari
items.description: The 19-year-old is remembered at a funeral on Vancouver Island as her parents call for an inquest into her death on Queensland's K'gari.

items.title: Almost 5 per cent of Tasmania's health budget spent on locum nurses
items.description: State government spending on locum nurses continues to rapidly rise, despite repeated calls to build a more permanent workforce.

items.title: Rain record broken, more wild weather expected in Victoria
items.description: Thunderstorms and heavy rain are expected to continue across Victoria.

items.title: A Melbourne dad was shot dead in Bali. The accused argue it was a debt 'scare' gone wrong
items.description: Three Australian men are waiting to be sentenced after a months-long trial for the alleged murder of a Melbourne father. Police say it was a deliberate hit job, while the men say it was not intentional.

items.title: How AI is levelling the playing field in the search for our next Olympians
items.description: A sliding doors moment can be all it takes to put someone on the path to elite sport. But those in charge of finding our next Olympians have a "world-first" idea to change that.

items.title: Sienna survived childhood cancer. Then, her heart began to fail
items.description: After overcoming cancer as a child, scans revealed her heart was "working under half of what it should".

items.title: History quiz: Can you work your way backward through these questions?
items.description: Where was MH370 heading, which Australian won our first Oscar and what was the world's first vampire movie?

items.title: The four stages of the mental load and the one men participate most in
items.description: While research has found mothers do more in all four stages of cognitive labour, there was one stage where men were more active than others.

items.title: Meet the Australians making the ultimate tree change
items.description: Moving to the country might sound idyllic to overstimulated and stressed-out city dwellers, but for Max and Courtney, it took some soul-searching to find their purpose and a place to really call home.

items.title: 'Their dirty secrets, not mine': Former prison officers speak out about NSW system
items.description: Current and former NSW prison officers describe what they say is a toxic workplace culture and a system that shields officers accused of serious misconduct, rather than holding them accountable. They argue it has driven younger officers out of the service.

items.title: Seventh narco sub found near Australian waters, signalling 'insane amount of drugs'
items.description: At least seven narco subs have been discovered in Pacific waters near Australia in the past 18 months, with experts warning that Australia's cocaine demand means more are on the way.

items.title: Inpex emissions 'systematically underestimated' since 2018, report finds
items.description: An independent review into oil and gas company Inpex has found widespread and persistent failures in how emissions were calculated, recorded and reported, dating back to the start of production in 2018.

items.title: How university life in Australia has changed
items.description: Two students who went to the same university 30 years apart share their radically different experiences as lectures go online and face-to-face contact takes a back seat in the post-pandemic world.

items.title: Crichton kicks golden-point winner to down Dragons in Vegas
items.description: Canterbury captain Stephen Crichton kicks a field goal to beat the Dragons 15-14 in golden point as the 2026 NRL season kicks off in Las Vegas.

items.title: Crocodiles spotted in Newcastle creek
items.description: Reptile experts are searching for several juvenile freshwater crocodiles that have been spotted in a New South Wales creek.

items.title: In PNG's highlands, a warlord points to a boy: 'He's one of my soldiers'
items.description: The proliferation of illegal high-powered guns is fuelling tribal warfare across Papua New Guinea and warlords claim children as young as eight are being trained to carry the weapons.

items.title: 'Shocking' reason behind 40pc of NSW's more than 200 kidnappings a year
items.description: Data shows that in the year to September 2025, NSW Police received 230 abduction and kidnapping reports — up from 224 in the previous year.

items.title: The Bondi terror attack changed how to buy a gun. Here's what it takes
items.description: Law reforms were swiftly passed following the massacre in December. So how difficult has it become  to legally own a firearm in the state?

items.title: Extreme rhetoric in right-wing political circles deserves more attention
items.description: The rhetoric in Australia's right-wing political circles is getting more extreme and the media should be paying more attention.
